items.title: Antonelli wins the United States GP on a one-stop; title decision deferred
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli converted pole into a ninth win of the season, 13.078s ahead of Charles Leclerc, with Max Verstappen third and Lewis Hamilton fourth. He ran a long medium stint then the hard to the flag while many rivals stopped twice; a late Virtual Safety Car, caused by Valtteri Bottas stopping, did not change the result. Bottas, Franco Colapinto and Ollie Bearman retired.
items.why_it_matters: Antonelli could not clinch the championship in Austin and carries the chance into Mexico City. The clinching scenario depends on his result relative to George Russell and Hamilton; check the current standings page for the exact permutations.

sources.label: The Race: Antonelli on the brink of first title

items.title: Russell struggles to P8 while Ferrari's upgrade delivers a podium but not the win
items.summary: Russell finished eighth and said he could not explain his race pace. Ferrari were fastest in practice with upgrades fitted and took second and fourth in the race; Formula1.com's Monday debrief examines how one lap cost Leclerc a shot at victory, and Hamilton singled out his 'biggest issue' of the race.
items.why_it_matters: Mercedes' two cars are no longer evenly matched, and Ferrari's practice pace did not convert into a win. This is a team and driver account, not an FIA finding.

sources.label: Formula1.com: Hamilton and Leclerc after the race

items.title: Lindblad, Colapinto, Bortoleto and Stroll all started behind their qualifying positions
items.summary: Arvid Lindblad started P14 while Colapinto and Bortoleto dropped to P20 and P21 after exceeding power-unit allocations; Bortoleto's drop was 80 places. Lance Stroll started from the pit lane after car modifications in parc ferme and extra PU elements. Bortoleto finished 13th.
items.why_it_matters: Penalty-driven starts explain several midfield results and show how stretched the 2026 PU allocations are late in the season.
